brief: Hot September core CPI (+0.33% MoM) briefly pushed the 10yr Treasury yield above 5.30%, but growth concerns and an AI-driven Nasdaq selloff (~4%) triggered a flight to quality that pulled 10s about 15bps lower to 5.07% by Friday, even as markets priced out an October Fed hike (GS Economics still expects an October pause then a December hike). This growth-versus-inflation tension is spilling into credit: index-level IG stayed calm (IG100 about 2bps wider) while AI-exposed names diverged sharply, with Oracle's long bonds widening about 43bps to +320, Oracle CDS widening 30-40bps, and CoreWeave's debt yields hitting 15%. CCC spreads breached 1,045bps even as BB demand and IG fund inflows ($1.06bn this week, $240.6bn YTD) held up. GS frames this as discrimination rather than retreat: capital still wants credit risk but is now pricing an issuer's ability to self-finance growth against dependence on continued financing, a distinction GIR extends to AI project finance, where a sample of HY data-center bond prices has fallen from $101.5 in June to $94.7 in October even as issuance is forecast to nearly triple by 2027. Idiosyncratic single-name stress (JetBlue, FMC, UWM) and loan-market resilience round out the dispersion story.
